key_insight: Applying the Agent Skill paradigm to small language models (SLMs) can meaningfully improve their reliability—reducing hallucinations and improving task accuracy—making SLMs more viable for industrial deployments where proprietary models are constrained.
problem_solved: Determines whether the Agent Skill framework’s benefits (better context engineering, lower hallucination, higher task accuracy) extend to SLMs, addressing industry needs for private, cost-effective, and dependable on-prem or edge-capable models.
method: Implement Agent Skill abstractions as a wrapper/agent layer for multiple SLMs to standardize prompts, tools, and context handling.
Benchmark SLMs with and without Agent Skills on representative industrial tasks, measuring task accuracy, hallucination rate, context utilization, latency, and resource cost.
Compare results against proprietary model baselines and analyze variance across tasks and model sizes to identify where Agent Skills help most.
impact: Shows a practical path for organizations to improve SLM performance and robustness without full dependence on external proprietary APIs—helpful for privacy, cost control, and on-prem adoption of AI agents in production.
visual_elements: Before/After bar chart: hallucination rate and task accuracy for SLMs with vs. without Agent Skills.
Architecture diagram: Agent Skill layer connecting task tools, context store, and an SLM, showing data/control flow.
Heatmap or matrix: task-by-model performance gains to highlight which tasks benefit most.
Cost/privacy infographic: trade-offs comparing external proprietary models vs. enhanced SLMs (latency, cost, data exposure).
paper_title: Agent Skill Framework: Perspectives on the Potential of Small Language Models in Industrial Environments
paper_authors: Yangjie Xu, Lujun Li, Lama Sleem, Niccolo Gentile, Yewei Song
